statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-102554 is fixed in Guava 33.7.2. The Guava copies reported here are embedded inside other jars and cannot be upgraded on their own: 14.0.1 inside ambari-metrics-common 2.7.0.0.0 (ambari-metrics-emitter extension), 30.1.1-jre shaded inside hadoop-client-runtime 3.3.6, and 33.2.1-jre (Druid 36) or 33.4.8-jre (Druid 37) inside iceberg-bundled-guava (druid-iceberg-extensions). The latest Iceberg release (iceberg-bundled-guava 1.12.0) still bundles Guava 33.7.1-jre, and the latest hadoop-client-runtime (3.5.0) bundles 33.4.8-jre. The issue requires Java deserialization of an attacker-crafted CompactHashMap, CompactHashSet or MapMakerInternalMap stream; reachability through these extensions has not been assessed. https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-xxph-c9ww-hj94

CVE-2026-102554 is fixed in Guava 33.7.2. The Guava copies reported here are embedded inside other jars and cannot be upgraded on their own: 14.0.1 inside ambari-metrics-common 2.7.0.0.0 (ambari-metrics-emitter extension), 30.1.1-jre shaded inside hadoop-client-runtime 3.3.6, 32.0.1-jre inside hadoop-shaded-guava 1.4.0 (druid-ranger-security), 32.1.3-jre shaded into the opentelemetry-emitter jar from that module's shade.guava.version, and 33.2.1-jre (Druid 36) or 33.4.8-jre (Druid 37) inside iceberg-bundled-guava (druid-iceberg-extensions). The latest Iceberg release (iceberg-bundled-guava 1.12.0) still bundles Guava 33.7.1-jre, and the latest hadoop-client-runtime (3.5.0) bundles 33.4.8-jre. hadoop-shaded-guava 1.6.0 bundles Guava 33.7.2-jre, and the opentelemetry-emitter property can be moved to 33.7.2-jre; images built before those pins still ship the versions listed here. Druid 38's managed guava.version pin is 33.5.0-jre, which is not one of those embedded copies; moving that pin to 33.7.2 requires a new druid-38 package revision. The issue requires Java deserialization of an attacker-crafted CompactHashMap, CompactHashSet or MapMakerInternalMap stream; reachability through these extensions has not been assessed. https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-xxph-c9ww-hj94

Guava 14.0.1 is relocated to org.sparkproject.guava inside org.apache.spark:spark-network-common_2.12, which spark-core pulls into every spark-dependencies job jar; the relocated copy includes MapMakerInternalMap, one of the classes named in the advisory. The unshaded Guava in the image is 33.7.2-jre. Maven dependency management cannot replace Guava inside Spark's shaded artifact, and no Spark release bundles a fixed Guava: the 3.5 line (3.5.8 and the latest, 3.5.9) embeds 14.0.1, and Spark 4.2.1 and 4.3.0 embed 33.6.0-jre while also requiring Scala 2.13. Remediation requires a Spark release that bundles Guava 33.7.2 or later. https://github.com/google/guava/releases/tag/v33.7.2

The remaining Guava 33.4.8-jre in the Data Prepper image is relocated inside iceberg-bundled-guava-1.10.1.jar, which Data Prepper's iceberg-source plugin depends on through Apache Iceberg 1.10.1. Gradle dependency resolution cannot replace Guava inside that shaded artifact. No Iceberg release on Maven Central bundles a fixed Guava yet: iceberg-bundled-guava 1.10.2 embeds 33.4.8-jre, 1.11.0 embeds 33.6.0-jre and 1.12.0 embeds 33.7.1-jre. Iceberg main moved to Guava 33.7.2-jre (https://github.com/apache/iceberg/pull/18453) and backports to the 1.10.x and 1.11.x lines are open (https://github.com/apache/iceberg/pull/18761, https://github.com/apache/iceberg/pull/18753). The unshaded Guava in the image is 33.7.2-jre and hadoop-shaded-guava is 1.6.0 (Guava 33.7.2-jre).

The DHI gradle-8 and gradle-9 Debian packages bundle com.google.guava:guava 33.7.2-jre on the distribution dependency platform. Google fixed CVE-2026-102554 in Guava 33.7.2 (https://github.com/google/guava/releases/tag/v33.7.2).

Ray 2.58.0 through 2.60.0 bundle Guava 32.0.1-jre. CVE-2026-102554 is fixed in 33.7.2-jre. Swapping that jar for 33.7.2 crosses Guava's 33 line, which changed finalization and several collection APIs, and that replacement is not validated against Ray's Java runtime. https://github.com/google/guava/releases/tag/v33.7.2

The NiFi image SBOM locates Guava 33.4.8-jre inside hadoop-shaded-guava-1.5.0.jar bundled in nifi-iceberg-parquet-writer-nar, and Guava 33.7.1-jre inside iceberg-bundled-guava-1.12.0.jar in nifi-iceberg-shared-nar. NiFi Maven dependency management cannot replace guava inside those shaded artifacts. org.apache.hadoop.thirdparty:hadoop-shaded-guava 1.5.0 is the latest Hadoop thirdparty release on Maven Central and still embeds Guava 33.4.8-jre; org.apache.iceberg:iceberg-bundled-guava 1.12.0 is the latest Iceberg bundled release and still embeds Guava 33.7.1-jre. Remediation requires upstream shaded releases that bundle Guava 33.7.2 or later.

The only remaining Guava 33.7.1-jre in the NiFi image is shaded inside iceberg-bundled-guava-1.12.0.jar, which ships in most NARs under /opt/nifi/nifi-current/lib and in /opt/nifi/nifi-toolkit-current/lib. org.apache.iceberg:iceberg-bundled-guava 1.12.0 is the latest Iceberg release on Maven Central and still embeds Guava 33.7.1-jre, and Maven dependency management cannot replace Guava inside that shaded artifact. Remediation requires an Iceberg release that bundles Guava 33.7.2 or later. The unshaded Guava in nifi-aws-service-api-nar is pinned to 33.7.2-jre, and nifi-iceberg-parquet-writer-nar now uses hadoop-shaded-guava 1.6.0 (Guava 33.7.2-jre) in place of 1.5.0 (Guava 33.4.8-jre).

Guava 33.7.2-jre contains the upstream fix, but overriding parent dependencyManagement to 33.7.2-jre breaks the persistence-cassandra-4.0 OSGi bundle at runtime (NoClassDefFoundError on InternalFutureFailureAccess from com.google.guava:failureaccess). graphql-java also shades guava 32.1.x inside its jar; no graphql-java release on Maven Central yet embeds 33.7.2-jre.

The Guava 33.6.0 copy relocated in iceberg-bundled-guava 1.11.0 is reached only through Java deserialization, and the admin tool deserializes no untrusted input: Polaris code never reads an ObjectInputStream, and the library readers present load only files the image or the tool itself writes.

Duplicate of CVE-2023-2976 (both affect Files.createTempDir()). See that entry for upgrade blocker.

Fixed in guava 32.0.0+. Bumping to 32.1.3-jre via parent dependencyManagement was attempted but fails at runtime: maven-bundle-plugin does not re-embed the sister artifact com.google.guava:failureaccess into the persistence-cassandra-4.0 OSGi bundle after the version override, causing Cassandra's Memtable flush to NoClassDefFoundError on InternalFutureFailureAccess. Will revisit when bundle embedding can be resolved or when stargate moves off maven-bundle-plugin 5.x.
